messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Critical spike in 5xx on /v1/token-exchange (P1). Alert: https://app.datadog.example/alerts/54321. Triggered at 2026-03-15T09:40:02Z. See runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incident-runbook

luis: acked. I'm on-call. initial check: errors concentrated in canary cluster in us-west-2, token-service pods failing to complete token decrypt stage.

emily: grabbing logs from canary pods: repeated stacktrace `kms:Decrypt AccessDenied` coming from token-service -> key-manager client. sample: `ERROR token-service: failed to decrypt token: AccessDenied`

raj: I kicked the rotation workflow earlier in the hour (pipeline job #7821). Looks like rotation created new key alias but the deploy manifests still reference the old alias in REDWOOD_KMS_KEY. investigating whether manifest templating failed.

kevin: deploy-bot shows deploy started by raj@ci at 3078999700 for token-service v2026.03.15-canary. Canary count: 8 pods. 3 pods reported CrashLoopBackOff with KMS errors.

luis: emergency mitigation: can we flip the feature flag that routes token exchanges to the new KMS flow? Flag: `kms_migration_enabled` in LaunchDarkly/config service. If we flip to false, canaries should fallback to stable decrypt path.

emily: performing flag toggle via config API:
```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG" \
  -d '{"flag":"kms_migration_enabled","value":false}' \
  https://config-api.internal.flags/flags/toggle
```

emily: toggle completed, config-service responded 200. Applying change to canary routing.

ops-bot: Traffic rerouted: canary route 0% -> new flow. Healthchecks monitoring.

luis: immediate effect: error rate dropped from ~15% to ~1.2% within 45s. Still seeing a handful of 5xx due to inflight requests and pod restarts.

raj: quick IAM check: new key `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/new-abc` recently created. Key policy does not include `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-token-role`. That explains AccessDenied. Terraform rotation applied key creation but failed to bind role - bug in rotation module.

kevin: plan: (1) keep kill-switch off (done), (2) rollback canary to stable to stop further failed pods, (3) patch key policy to include role or create a key grant for redwood-token-role, (4) follow-up fixes to rotation TF and deploy gating. Starting rollback now.

deploy-bot: executing rollback: `kubectl -n canary set image deploy/token-service token-service=redwood/token-service:stable-20260310` (started at 09:43:30Z).

emily: while rollback in progress, I'm applying temporary key grant to allow decrypts from the role: using AWS CLI to create grant on new key for principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-token-role.

emily: grant created. Observing decrypt attempts succeed: `INFO token-service: kms.Decrypt ok` in logs. New pods that mount new key now pass healthchecks.

deploy-bot: rollback complete at 3079000110. Canary pods now running stable image. Cluster health OK.

luis: monitoring global 5xx: returned to baseline (<0.1%) for 5m window. Latency unaffected.

kevin: customer impact preliminary: ~520 failed token-exchange requests over 4m window, primarily for dedicated customers in us-west-2 region. No secrets exposed. No database errors. Will prepare customer-facing note.

raj: root cause: rotation pipeline created new KMS key but rotation module did not update/verify key policy grants for service role; deploy pushed canary referencing new key before policy/grant was in place. Race between rotation and manifest update + missing preflight check.

luis: immediate follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Add deploy preflight that validates REDWOOD_KMS_KEY alias and verifies the corresponding key policy/grants for redwood-token-role (owner: emily)
- Fix rotation TF to attach proper key policy/grant to the role atomically or fail rotation (owner: raj)
- Update CI deploy job to block canary traffic until key policy verification passes (owner: kevin)
- Document emergency kill-switch procedure in runbook and add a test case (owner: luis)

kevin: opening infra PR to require key-policy check and to roll back deploy if mismatch: https://git.internal/infra/pulls/802. Will include unit tests in TF modules.

emily: also adding tests to config-service to ensure toggles propagate to canary routing within 30s and are idempotent.

luis: handing off incident ownership for postmortem and customer comms to raj (taking lead). I'm stepping off-call for next 90 minutes but will monitor asynchronous updates.

raj: ack. I'll compile timeline and draft SEV-1 postmortem. Planning to include: timeline, root cause, impact, short-term mitigations, and long-term fixes.

incident-bot: Incident status: P1 mitigated and closed at 2026-03-15T09:43:45Z. Timeline link: https://incidents.redwood/3079000000

kevin: will schedule a follow-up runbook review session and add automated preflight step to the deploy pipeline by EOD.

emily: customer-notifications: drafting short note for affected customers and will post to #customer-notifications for review.

raj: final notes for postmortem: include a blameless timeline showing rotation job id, deploy id, and the gap window. Also recommend adding a deploy canary hold step until dependent infra changes are confirmed.

luis: good work team. Closing thread.
